  1897	## FiniteWick (whole result)
  1898	
  1899	A reusable foundation with no manuscript label of its own, proved in full with
  1900	nothing supplied. It formalizes the Wick (Isserlis) step in the proof of
  1901	`L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at
  1902	`a284420`): the formula `E:terminal-wick-formula` (lines 3619-3622) with "each
  1903	pairing has coefficient one" and "if `m+n` is odd, the expectation is zero"
  1904	(line 3638), the Gaussian moment computation of the proof (lines 3662-3675), the
  1905	moment bound of lines 3651-3656, and the pointwise positivity and comparison of
  1906	covariance products (lines 3693-3695). The chain integrals themselves are in
  1907	`TerminalWick`. Abstractions: a pairing (pair partition) of a finite set `S` of a
  1908	linearly ordered finite type is a fixed-point-free involution of `S`, normalized
  1909	to the identity off `S` so that each pair partition is exactly one function
  1910	(`pairings`); its weight takes one factor `c(a, p a)` per pair, at the smaller
  1911	element `a < p a`, so every unordered pair contributes once with coefficient one
  1912	(`pairWeight`); `wickSum c S` is the sum of the weights. For `S` all of
  1913	`Fin (2k)` these are the pair partitions `Pi_k` of the TeX. The double factorial
  1914	is `Nat.doubleFactorial` with natural subtraction, so `(2*0-1)!! = 0!! = 1`, the
  1915	empty-product convention of line 3639. Gaussian side: `stdPi N` (from
  1916	`GaussianIBP`) is the law of `N` independent standard Gaussians, and Mathlib
  1917	defines `multivariateGaussian 0 K` as the image of the standard Gaussian under
  1918	`x -> sqrt(K) x` (`CFC.sqrt`). `CenteredGaussianField W K P` states the TeX's
  1919	hypothesis "centered real Gaussian field with covariance `K`" (lines 3601-3602)
  1920	as: for every finite family of points `p : Fin n -> X`, the matrix
  1921	`(K(p_a, p_b))` is positive semidefinite and `(W(p_a))_a` has law
  1922	`multivariateGaussian 0 (K(p_a, p_b))`. Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
  1923	`K` positive semidefinite (otherwise Mathlib's `multivariateGaussian 0 K` is the
  1924	Dirac mass at `0`), and every integral identity for Gaussian monomials (products
  1925	of finitely many coordinates or field values) comes with the integrability of
  1926	its integrand as a conjunct. The exception is the bridge
  1927	`integral_multivariateGaussian_eq` for an arbitrary continuous `F`: it is an
  1928	equality of Lean's totalized integrals and assumes no integrability, so for a
  1929	non-integrable `F` (for instance `exp(x_0^4)` under a nondegenerate Gaussian)
  1930	both sides are the junk value `0`; integrability transfers only through the
  1931	separate equivalence `integrable_multivariateGaussian_iff`. No hypothesis is carried unused. Proof-route
  1932	differences: the Gaussian identity is proved by Stein's recursion
  1933	`E[g_e F(g)] = E[partial_e F(g)]` (`GaussianIBP.integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth`)
  1934	for `x = A g`, expanded along the partner of the least index
  1935	(`wickSum_eq_sum_erase`), instead of differentiating the moment generating
  1936	function (lines 3664-3673); the conclusion is the same. The moment bound
  1937	`E(prod_{a<n} W(p_a))^2 <= (2n-1)!! V^n` (`CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le`)
  1938	is the Wick formula for the `2n` values together with the count of `(2k-1)!!`
  1939	pairings (`card_pairings_even`, `wickSum_abs_le`) and `|K(x,y)| <= V`
  1940	(`CenteredGaussianField.abs_le`), instead of Hoelder's inequality and `L^(2n)`
  1941	Gaussian moments; the bound is the same. No conclusion is narrower than the
  1942	TeX step it formalizes. Junk values: `wickSum` is a finite sum, and every Bochner
  1943	integral of a Gaussian monomial appears with a proof of integrability; only the
  1944	continuous-`F` bridge above can equate two junk values, and the monomial
  1945	results apply it to integrable monomials. Refutations
  1946	(`refutations/finite-wick/`), all combinatorial or one-dimensional controls
  1947	without junk-value reliance: `PairingCount` (`(2k)!/k!` pairings of a `2k`-set;
  1948	`k = 2` gives `12`, not `3`), `AbsBound` (the pairing-sum bound without
  1949	`(2k-1)!!`; `c = 1` on `Fin 4`), `NonnegDropped` (pairing sums nonnegative for
  1950	arbitrary real weights, not a covariance; `c = -1` on `Fin 2`) and
  1951	`FourthMoment` (`E x^4 = 1` for a standard Gaussian `x`, an actual Gaussian
  1952	law; the Wick formula gives `3`). Not
  1953	formalized here: everything about the chain measures, the `L^2`-valued integrals
  1954	and the series (see `TerminalWick`). The four route definitions `unpair`,
  1955	`pairUp`, `matBound` and `monoDeriv` are public but are not listed as claims;
  1956	they appear only inside the statements of the auxiliary rows below.

5911	## TerminalWick (whole result)
  5912	
  5913	Formalizes `L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  5914	at `a284420`; the chain measure `E:terminal-chain-measure`, lines 3585-3598; the
  5915	statement, lines 3600-3645, with the displays `E:terminal-term-majorant`
  5916	(3611-3615), `E:terminal-wick-formula` (3619-3622) and
  5917	`E:terminal-pairing-integral` (3624-3637); the proof, lines 3647-3699), built on
  5918	`FiniteWick`, with every stated conclusion proved for real `r` and two inputs
  5919	left outside Lean, and one added hypothesis (3). (1) Supplied: `hmeas`, the a.e. strong measurability of
  5920	`z -> prod_j W(z_j)` as an `L^2(Omega)`-valued map for each `nu n`. In the TeX it
  5921	follows from the cell-wise mean-square continuity ("the product is strongly
  5922	measurable in `L^2` on the stated pieces", lines 3657-3659); it is assumed here,
  5923	almost everywhere only, so it is no stronger than the TeX's claim. (2) Not
  5924	constructed: the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}`. The general theorems take
  5925	arbitrary finite measures `nu n` on `n`-tuples of points; the wrappers take
  5926	finite measures on `n`-tuples of points of `[0,T] x R^d` (`Pt d T`) with total
  5927	mass `chainMass d n T`. `chainMass d n T` is the lower integral of
  5928	`chainWeight d n T`, the recursion on the last vertex of
  5929	`1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) prod_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(R^d)` with `s_{n+1} = T` and the wave
  5930	Green measures `WaveGreen.waveGreen d` (in `d = 3` the module's documented
  5931	choice of surface measure). Lean proves `chainMass d n T = T^(2n)/(2n)!` for
  5932	`d in {1,2,3}`, `T >= 0` (`chainMass_eq`, from `G_h(R^d) = h` and the recursion
  5933	`M_{n+1}(T) = int_0^T (T-t) M_n(t) dt`, lines 3648-3651), but not that this is
  5934	the total mass of the measure `E:terminal-chain-measure` (a Tonelli and
  5935	pushforward identity), since that measure is not built. Only the total masses of
  5936	the `nu n` are used, so every conclusion holds for any finite measures with
  5937	these masses, in particular for `g_n^{T,x}` once constructed; the point `x`
  5938	enters only through the measures. (3) Added restriction, not in the
  5939	manuscript: `hK`, the joint (Borel) measurability of `(p, q) -> K p q` on
  5940	pairs of points of `[0,T] x R^d`, a hypothesis of `mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings`,
  5941	`integrable_pairWeight` and `terminal_wick_paper`, used only to split the
  5942	integral of the pairing sum into the separate pairing integrals and to prove
  5943	each pairing integrand integrable. The TeX assumes bounded variance and joint
  5944	mean-square continuity only on the open cells of a finite partition of
  5945	`[0,T]`; these leave the covariance at the cut times unrestricted, so `hK`
  5946	does not follow from them (a field that vanishes off one cut time `c` and
  5947	equals `1_A(y) Z` there, with `A` not Borel and `Z` standard Gaussian, meets
  5948	every TeX hypothesis and the supplied `hmeas`, but its covariance is not
  5949	measurable). The wrapper is therefore narrower than the lemma by this
  5950	restriction; `terminal_wick_mono_paper`, `mixed_moment_odd`,
  5951	`mixed_moment_nonneg` and `terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` do not take it. `Y_n` is `chainIntegral nu hW n`, the
  5952	Bochner integral in Mathlib's `Lp R 2 P` of `prodL2 hW z`, the `L^2` class of
  5953	`prod_j W(z_j)`; `E[Y_m Y_n]` is the integral of `Y_m(omega) Y_n(omega)`, equal to

  6369	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  6370	at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
  6371	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
  6372	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  6373	3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  6374	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  6375	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  6376	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  6377	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  6378	complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  6379	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  6380	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  6381	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  6382	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  6383	two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
  6384	nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
  6385	proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
  6386	`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
  6387	identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
  6388	not formalized. The
  6389	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  6390	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  6391	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  6392	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  6393	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  6394	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  6395	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  6396	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  6397	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  6398	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  6399	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  6400	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  6401	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  6402	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`

     7	file `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at revision a284420:

     9	statement (lines 3600-3645) and the proof (lines 3647-3699).  Built on the
    10	finite Wick foundation `FiniteWick`.
    11	
    12	Formalized:
    13	* The masses (lines 3648-3651): `chainMass d n T = ∫ 1_{[0,T]^n_<} ∏ G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(ℝ^d) ds`
    14	  equals `T^{2n}/(2n)!` for `T ≥ 0`, `d ∈ {1,2,3}` (`chainMass_eq`; recursion at
    15	  the last vertex `chainMassReal_succ`, wave Green masses from
    16	  `WaveGreen.waveGreen_mass`).
    17	* The terms `Y_n = ∫ ∏_j W(s_j, y_j) ν_n(ds, dy)` as `L²(Ω)`-valued Bochner
    18	  integrals (`prodL2`, `chainIntegral`), their existence (`integrable_prodL2`),
    19	  `Y_0 = 1` (`chainIntegral_zero`) and the majorant `E:terminal-term-majorant`
    20	  (`norm_chainIntegral_le`, with `√V^n = V^{n/2}`).
    21	* `E:terminal-wick-formula` with `E:terminal-pairing-integral`
    22	  (`mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings`, `pairingIntegral`; via `inner_chainIntegral`),
    23	  zero for odd `m + n` (`mixed_moment_odd`), nonnegativity of every pairing
    24	  integral and of every mixed moment when `K ≥ 0` (`pairing_integral_nonneg`,
    25	  `mixed_moment_nonneg`), entrywise monotonicity for `0 ≤ K₁ ≤ K₂`
    26	  (`mixed_moment_mono`), absolute convergence of `Σ r^n Y_n` in `L²` for every
    27	  real `r` (`summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral`).
    28	* Discharge of both fields of `UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput` for every
    29	  real `r` when `K ≥ 0` (`terminalWickInput_of_nonneg`; in the wrapper's last
    30	  conjunct).
    31	* Wrappers `terminal_wick_paper` and `terminal_wick_mono_paper` (the TeX's
    32	  hypotheses plus the added restriction `hK` and the supplied inputs below).
    33	
    34	The general theorems are stated for an arbitrary measurable point set `X`, a
    35	centered real Gaussian field (`FiniteWick.CenteredGaussianField`), a variance
    36	bound `K(x,x) ≤ V` and arbitrary finite measures `ν n` on `n`-tuples of points.
    37	The wrappers take `X = [0,T] × ℝ^d` (`Pt d T`), `V = sup_p K(p,p)` with
    38	`BddAbove` (the TeX's `V < ∞`, so `⨆` is a genuine supremum), and the chain
    39	measures `ν n` with total mass `chainMass d n T`.
    40	
    41	Supplied inputs (named hypotheses; no conclusion is assumed):
    42	* `hmeas` (TeX lines 3657-3659, "the product is strongly measurable in `L²` on
    43	  the stated pieces"): `z ↦ prodL2 hW z` is a.e. strongly measurable for
    44	  `ν n`.  In the TeX this follows from the mean-square continuity on cells;
    45	  here it is assumed, a.e. only, so it is no stronger than the TeX claim.
    46	* The chain measures `ν n` are not constructed in Lean.  The wrappers take them
    47	  as finite measures on `n`-tuples of points of `[0,T] × ℝ^d` with
    48	  `hmass : ν n (total) = chainMass d n T`, the total mass that the definition
    49	  `E:terminal-chain-measure` gives by Tonelli (pushforwards preserve mass).
    50	  Only this mass is used; every conclusion therefore holds for any finite
    51	  measures with these masses, in particular for `g_n^{T,x}`.
    52	
    53	Added restriction, not in the manuscript: global measurability of `K` on pairs
    54	of points (`hK`, used only to split the integral of the pairing sum into the
    55	separate pairing integrals of the formula).  The TeX's hypotheses (mean-square
    56	continuity on the open cells only) do not imply it: a field that is a
    57	non-Borel function of the space variable at one cut time satisfies them.
    58	
    59	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the covariance matrices of the field are
    60	positive semidefinite (part of `CenteredGaussianField`); `IsFiniteMeasure (ν n)`;
    61	`BddAbove` of the variances; `T > 0`.  Every integral conclusion comes with its
    62	integrability (`integrable_prodL2`, `integrable_pairWeight`).
    63

   106	/-- The integrand of the total mass of the terminal-chain measure
   107	`g_n^{T,x}` (`E:terminal-chain-measure`, main TeX lines 3585-3598), written by
   108	recursion on the last vertex: `chainWeight d 0 T () = 1` and
   109	`chainWeight d (n+1) T s = 1_{0 < s_{n+1} < T} G_{T - s_{n+1}}(ℝ^d) ·
   110	chainWeight d n s_{n+1} (s_1, …, s_n)`, i.e. `1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) ∏_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(ℝ^d)`
   111	with `s_{n+1} = T` and the open ordered simplex `0 < s_1 < ⋯ < s_n < T`
   112	(boundary null).  The spatial pushforward under `y_j = x - Σ_{l ≥ j} w_l`
   113	preserves mass, so `∫ chainWeight d n T = g_n^{T,x}(total)` for every `x`
   114	(Tonelli); the measure `g_n^{T,x}` itself is not constructed in Lean. -/
   115	def chainWeight (d : ℕ) : (n : ℕ) → ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞
   116	  | 0, _, _ => 1
   117	  | n + 1, T, s =>
   118	    (if 0 < s (Fin.last n) ∧ s (Fin.last n) < T then waveGreen d (T - s (Fin.last n)) univ else 0) *
   119	      chainWeight d n (s (Fin.last n)) (Fin.init s)
   120	
   121	/-- Auxiliary (Lean proof route): `chainWeight` with `G_h(ℝ^d)` replaced by `h`. -/
   122	def chainWeightReal : (n : ℕ) → ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞
   123	  | 0, _, _ => 1
   124	  | n + 1, T, s =>
   125	    (if 0 < s (Fin.last n) ∧ s (Fin.last n) < T then ENNReal.ofReal (T - s (Fin.last n)) else 0) *
   126	      chainWeightReal n (s (Fin.last n)) (Fin.init s)
   127	
   128	/-- Auxiliary: `G_h(ℝ^d) = h` for `h > 0` (`WaveGreen.waveGreen_mass`) identifies the two weights. -/
   129	theorem chainWeight_eq (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) :
   130	    ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (s : Fin n → ℝ), chainWeight d n T s = chainWeightReal n T s := by
   131	  intro n
   132	  induction n with
   133	  | zero => intro T s; rfl
   134	  | succ n ih =>
   135	    intro T s
   136	    simp only [chainWeight, chainWeightReal, ih]
   137	    congr 1
   138	    split_ifs with h
   139	    · exact waveGreen_mass d hd _ (by linarith [h.2])
   140	    · rfl
   141	
   142	/-- Auxiliary: joint measurability of `(T, s) ↦ chainWeightReal n T s`. -/
   143	theorem measurable_chainWeightReal (n : ℕ) :
   144	    Measurable fun p : ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) => chainWeightReal n p.1 p.2 := by
   145	  induction n with
   146	  | zero => exact measurable_const
   147	  | succ n ih =>
   148	    simp only [chainWeightReal]
   149	    have hlast : Measurable fun p : ℝ × (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) => p.2 (Fin.last n) :=
   150	      (measurable_pi_apply _).comp measurable_snd
   151	    have hinit : Measurable fun p : ℝ × (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) => Fin.init p.2 :=
   152	      measurable_pi_iff.mpr fun i => (measurable_pi_apply _).comp measurable_snd
   153	    refine Measurable.mul ?_ (ih.comp (hlast.prodMk hinit))
   154	    refine Measurable.ite ?_ (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (measurable_fst.sub hlast))
   155	      measurable_const
   156	    exact (measurableSet_lt measurable_const hlast).inter (measurableSet_lt hlast measurable_fst)
   157	
   158	/-- Auxiliary (Lean proof route): `∫ chainWeightReal n T`. -/
   159	def chainMassReal (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ := ∫⁻ s, chainWeightReal n T s
   160	
   161	/-- Integration at the last vertex (TeX lines 3648-3650):
   162	`M_{n+1}(T) = ∫_0^T (T - s) M_n(s) ds`. -/
   163	theorem chainMassReal_succ (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
   164	    chainMassReal (n + 1) T = ∫⁻ t in Ioo 0 T, ENNReal.ofReal (T - t) * chainMassReal n t := by
   165	  unfold chainMassReal
   166	  have hmp := measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => (volume : Measure ℝ))
   167	    (Fin.last n)
   168	  have hvol : (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => (volume : Measure ℝ)) = volume := rfl
   169	  set e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ) (Fin.last n)
   170	  set F : ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞ := fun p =>
   171	    (if 0 < p.1 ∧ p.1 < T then ENNReal.ofReal (T - p.1) else 0) * chainWeightReal n p.1 p.2 with hF
   172	  have hf : ∀ s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ, chainWeightReal (n + 1) T s = F (e s) := by
   173	    intro s
   174	    simp [chainWeightReal, hF, e, MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove_apply]
   175	  calc ∫⁻ s, chainWeightReal (n + 1) T s = ∫⁻ s, F (e s) ∂(Measure.pi fun _ => volume) :=
   176	        lintegral_congr hf
   177	    _ = ∫⁻ p, F p ∂((volume : Measure ℝ).prod (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => (volume : Measure ℝ))) :=
   178	        hmp.lintegral_comp_emb e.measurableEmbedding F
   179	    _ = _ := ?_
   180	  rw [show (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => (volume : Measure ℝ)) = volume from rfl]
   181	  rw [lintegral_prod _ ?_]
   182	  · rw [← lintegral_indicator measurableSet_Ioo]
   183	    refine lintegral_congr fun t => ?_
   184	    by_cases ht : t ∈ Ioo 0 T
   185	    · rw [indicator_of_mem ht]
   186	      simp only [hF, ite_eq_left (show 0 < t ∧ t < T from ht)]
   187	      exact lintegral_const_mul _ ((measurable_chainWeightReal n).comp measurable_prodMk_left)
   188	    · rw [indicator_of_notMem ht]
   189	      simp only [hF, ite_eq_right (show ¬ (0 < t ∧ t < T) from ht), zero_mul, lintegral_const]
   190	  · refine Measurable.aemeasurable (Measurable.mul ?_ (measurable_chainWeightReal n))
   191	    refine Measurable.ite ?_ (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (measurable_const.sub measurable_fst))
   192	      measurable_const
   193	    exact (measurableSet_lt measurable_const measurable_fst).inter
   194	      (measurableSet_lt measurable_fst measurable_const)

   196	/-- `M_n(T) = T^{2n}/(2n)!` for `T ≥ 0` (TeX lines 3650-3651), by induction. -/
   197	theorem chainMassReal_eq (n : ℕ) : ∀ T : ℝ, 0 ≤ T →
   198	    chainMassReal n T = ENNReal.ofReal (T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial) := by
   199	  induction n with

   201	  | succ n ih =>

   203	    rw [chainMassReal_succ]
   204	    rw [setLIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioo (g := fun t => ENNReal.ofReal
   205	      ((T - t) * (t ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial))) (fun t ht => by
   206	        rw [ih t ht.1.le, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by linarith [ht.2])])]

   213	      simp_rw [this]
   214	      rw [intervalIntegral.integral_div, intervalIntegral.integral_sub, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,
   215	        integral_pow, integral_pow]
   216	      · rw [show 2 * (n + 1) = 2 * n + 2 by ring, Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.factorial_succ]

    68	fixed-point-free involutions of `S`: maps `p : ι → ι` with `p x ∈ S`, `p x ≠ x`,

   652	theorem CenteredGaussianField.wick (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → X)
   653	    (j : ι → Fin n) (S : Finset ι) :
   654	    Integrable (fun ω => ∏ i ∈ S, W (p (j i)) ω) P ∧
   655	      ∫ ω, ∏ i ∈ S, W (p (j i)) ω ∂P = wickSum (fun a b => K (p (j a)) (p (j b))) S := by
   656	  have h := wick_hasLaw _ (hW.psd n p) _ (hW.law n p) j S
   657	  simpa using h

   659	/-- The Wick formula for `n` field values: `E ∏_a W(p_a) = Σ_{D ∈ Π(n)} ∏ K`. -/
   660	theorem CenteredGaussianField.wick_univ (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) {n : ℕ}
   661	    (p : Fin n → X) :
   662	    Integrable (fun ω => ∏ a, W (p a) ω) P ∧
   663	      ∫ ω, ∏ a, W (p a) ω ∂P = wickSum (fun a b => K (p a) (p b)) Finset.univ :=
   664	  CenteredGaussianField.wick hW p (id : Fin n → Fin n) Finset.univ

   667	theorem CenteredGaussianField.symm (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) (x y : X) :
   668	    K y x = K x y := by
   669	  have h := (hW.psd 2 ![x, y]).isHermitian.apply 0 1
   670	  simpa using h

   672	/-- `|K(x,y)| ≤ V` when `K(z,z) ≤ V` for every `z` (positive semidefiniteness at
   673	the two points `x, y`; Lean route for the variance bound). -/
   674	theorem CenteredGaussianField.abs_le (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) (V : ℝ)
   675	    (hV : ∀ x, K x x ≤ V) (x y : X) : |K x y| ≤ V := by
   676	  have hpsd := hW.psd 2 ![x, y]
   677	  have h1 := hpsd.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg ![1, -1]
   678	  have h2 := hpsd.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg ![1, 1]
   679	  have hs := hW.symm x y
   680	  simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two] at h1 h2
   681	  have := hV x
   682	  have := hV y
   683	  rw [_root_.abs_le]
   684	  constructor <;> nlinarith

   687	`p : Fin m → X`, `q : Fin n → X`,
   688	`E[∏_a W(p_a) ∏_b W(q_b)] = Σ_{D ∈ Π(m+n)} ∏_{{a,b} ∈ D} K(τ_a, τ_b)` with
   689	`τ = Fin.append p q`, and the product is integrable. -/
   690	theorem CenteredGaussianField.wick_append (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) {m n : ℕ}
   691	    (p : Fin m → X) (q : Fin n → X) :
   692	    Integrable (fun ω => (∏ a, W (p a) ω) * ∏ b, W (q b) ω) P ∧
   693	      ∫ ω, (∏ a, W (p a) ω) * ∏ b, W (q b) ω ∂P =
   694	        wickSum (fun a b => K (Fin.append p q a) (Fin.append p q b)) Finset.univ := by
   695	  have h := hW.wick_univ (Fin.append p q)
   696	  have heq : ∀ ω, ∏ i, W (Fin.append p q i) ω = (∏ a, W (p a) ω) * ∏ b, W (q b) ω := by
   697	    intro ω; rw [Fin.prod_univ_add]; simp
   698	  simp_rw [heq] at h
   699	  exact h

   701	/-- The moment bound behind `E:terminal-term-majorant` (main TeX lines
   702	3651-3656): if `K(z,z) ≤ V` for every `z`, then
   703	`E(∏_{a<n} W(p_a))² ≤ (2n-1)!! V^n`.  Lean route: the Wick formula for the
   704	`2n` values and `wickSum_abs_le` (`(2n-1)!!` pairings, each at most `V^n` in
   705	absolute value), instead of the TeX's Hölder inequality and `L^{2n}` Gaussian
   706	moments; same bound. -/
   707	theorem CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) (V : ℝ)
   708	    (hV : ∀ x, K x x ≤ V) {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → X) :
   709	    Integrable (fun ω => (∏ a, W (p a) ω) ^ 2) P ∧
   710	      ∫ ω, (∏ a, W (p a) ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ((2 * n - 1).doubleFactorial : ℝ) * V ^ n := by
   711	  obtain ⟨hi, he⟩ := hW.wick_append p p
   712	  simp_rw [sq]
   713	  refine ⟨hi, ?_⟩
   714	  rw [he]
   715	  refine (le_abs_self _).trans ?_
   716	  exact wickSum_abs_le _ V (fun a b => hW.abs_le V hV _ _) n _ (by simp; ring)
   717

    69	theorem norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg (v : ℕ → E) (S : E) (hS : HasSum v S)

    94	theorem term_bound (Y : ℕ → E) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r)
    95	    (hsum : Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • Y n‖)
    96	    (hpos : ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y m) (Y n))
    97	    (hB : ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B) (n : ℕ) :

   108	  have h' : r ^ n * ‖Y n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B := by

   224	  rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, L2.inner_def]
   225	  congr 1

   229	/-- Supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (TeX lines 3600-3645 at a284420; the two facts at 3638-3644), for

   236	structure TerminalWickInput (μ : Measure Ω) (Y : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (r : ℝ) : Prop where

  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]

  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}

  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then

  3685	  In dimension three one may first replace $G$ by $p_\eta*G$. Those positive
  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}
  3700	
  3701	\subsection{Removing the regularization}
  3702	
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
  3728	
  3729	\begin{proof}
  3730	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3731	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3732	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3736	  absolute convergence.
  3737	
  3738	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3739	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3740	  \[
  3741	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3742	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3743	  \]
  3744	  First let $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$ at fixed $N$, and then let $N \to
  3745	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3746	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3747	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3748	\end{proof}

   803	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   804	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   805	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   806	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   807	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   808	  \[
   809	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   810	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   811	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   812	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   813	  \]
   814	  Let
   815	  \[
   816	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   817	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   818	  \]
   819	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   820	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   821	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   822	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   823	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   824	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   825	  \end{equation}
   826	  More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   827	  $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   828	  by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   829	  $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   830	  and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   831	  \[
   832	    K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   833	    \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   834	  \]
   835	  Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   836	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   837	    \begin{split}
   838	      0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   839	      0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   840	    \end{split}
   841	  \end{equation}

    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
    64	  onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
    65	  $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
    66	  operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
    67	  displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
    68	  of a general distributional velocity is taken.
    69	
    70	  In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
    71	  \[
    72	    W_t(\xi)=
    73	    \begin{pmatrix}
    74	      \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
    75	      -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
    76	    \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
    77	  \]
    78	  At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
    79	  the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
    80	  $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
    81	  $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
    84	  Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
    85	  Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
    86	  generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
    87	
    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
    89	  Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
    90	  $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
    91	  Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
    93	  proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
    94	  $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
    95	  \[
    96	    \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
    97	  \]
    98	  is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
    99	  of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   100	  in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   101	  that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   102	
   103	  We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   104	  Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   105	  $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   106	  transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   107	  integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   108	  function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by
   109	  parts for the approximants, proves $\langle\tau_yz,w\rangle_E \to 0$ as $|y|
   110	  \to \infty$. Thus, $\tau_yz$ tends weakly to zero. For compact $K$,
   111	  $\|K\tau_yz\| \to 0$: otherwise compactness supplies a norm-convergent
   112	  subsequence with nonzero norm, while bounded linear testing makes its limit
   113	  zero. For unit $z$ it follows that
   114	  \[
   115	    \|S_E(h)+K\|
   116	    \ge\liminf_{|y|\to\infty}\|(S_E(h)+K)\tau_yz\|
   117	    \ge\|S_E(h)z\|.
   118	  \]
   119	  Taking the supremum over $z$ gives $\|S_E(h)+K\| \ge \|S_E(h)\|$. The
   120	  isometric velocity reversal $\mathcal{R}(u,v) = (u,-v)$ satisfies $S_E(-h) =
   121	  \mathcal{R} S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$ by the full free Fourier matrix. The group law
   122	  yields $1 \le \|S_E(-h)\|\|S_E(h)\| = \|S_E(h)\|^2$. This
   123	  proves~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}.
   124	
   125	  Finally, $P_j-S_E(\ell_j)$ is compact. Telescoping the finite ordered product
   126	  against its free product gives a finite sum of bounded--compact--bounded
   127	  products, hence a compact difference. Only the free factors are combined by
   128	  the group law; no noisy factors are commuted. The same translation argument
   129	  proves \eqref{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}. A zero length gives $P_j
   130	  = I$. All assertions are at fixed finite horizons and products; no uniform
   131	  compact approximation in a radius, horizon or number of factors is asserted.
   132	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:symplectic-free}.
   133	\end{proof}

   225	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   226	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   227	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   228	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   229	  convention
   230	  \[
   231	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   232	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   233	  \]
   234	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   235	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   236	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   237	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   238	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   239	  \end{equation}
   240	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   241	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   242	\end{hypothesis}
   526	expansion~\eqref{E:expansion} with initial data $(1,0)$, and $\kappa$ is the
   527	exponent in~\eqref{E:kappa}. The spectral measure $\mu$ has the normalization
   528	specified in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. Write $B_1$ for the unit ball in
   529	$\R^d$, and put
   530	\begin{equation}\label{E:intro-spectral-mass}
   531	  R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi\mu(B_1)}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)}.
   532	\end{equation}
   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}
   103	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, allowing $\Gamma=0$, let
   104	  $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   105	  $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   106	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   107	    0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   108	    \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.
   111	\end{lemma}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  If $b=0$, smoothness makes $\nabla g=0$ everywhere. Thus, $g$ is constant,
   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]
   120	  In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   125	  \]
   126	  is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]
   134	  Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]
   145	  Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   148	  \]
   149	  The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   151	  with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   152	  \[
   153	    \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]
   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}

    23	  \label{L:positive-raw-embedding}
    24	  For any real Hilbert space $G$ there is a bounded map $J_G:L^2(I;G) \to
    25	  H_t\otimes G$ with
    26	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}
    27	    \|J_GF\|^2
    28	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle F(s),F(t)\rangle_G\ud s\ud t
    29	    \le K_0\|F\|_{L^2(I;G)}^2,\qquad K_0=\frac{2^a}{1-a}.
    30	  \end{equation}
    31	  The natural inclusion puts every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ in
    32	  $H_I$, with
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-raw-mean}
    34	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2=v_\Psi,\qquad
    35	    \mathcal{T}_R\Psi(s)=B_E(m_Rh_{\Psi,s})\quad\hbox{a.e. }s.
    36	  \end{equation}
    37	  For each fixed smooth $\Psi$ the right side gives a canonical version for
    38	  every $R \ge 1$ and every $s \in I$.
